data.goal: Make 'origin doctor' read the push credential it reports (T-0024)

data.summary: $ python3 /tmp/opencode/falsify-doctor-current.py

Falsification run 1: the obvious functional probe (git ls-remote) is vacuous here because the remote is public; 'git credential fill' is rejected by this App arrangement. Discovered the live defect: ~/.config/github-app/git-credential-helper.sh on this VM still invokes /tmp/github-app-jwt.sh, the exact /tmp dependency STATE.md records as having broken pushes on instance-20260717-0947, and doctor prints 'credentials none present' while the mechanism is one /tmp clear away from failing.

argv: printf "[credential]\n\thelper = %s\n" "$HOME/.config/github-app/git-credential-helper.sh"; echo "helper mode: $(stat -c %a "$HOME/.config/github-app/git-credential-helper.sh")"; echo "jwt script:  $(stat -c %a /tmp/github-app-jwt.sh 2>&1) at /tmp/github-app-jwt.sh"; ls "$HOME/.config/github-app/"
data.summary: $ sh -c printf "[credential]\n\thelper = %s\n" "$HOME/.config/github-app/git-credential-helper.sh"; echo "helper mode: $(stat -c %a "$HOME/.co

I overwrote this VM's ~/.gitconfig while building the T-0024 falsification harness: two of its three cases passed Path.home() as the sandbox HOME, so the harness wrote its throwaway gitconfig over the real one and destroyed user.name, user.email, and credential.helper. Repaired from the values read earlier in the same session (bot identity confirmed against 125 committed commits); git credential fill now exits 0. The harness caused it, not the environment: my first reading of the 'invalid credential line' error blamed the App arrangement, and that reading was wrong - the corrupted gitconfig pointed credential.helper at /tmp/github-app-jwt.sh, a JWT generator that is not a credential helper, which is exactly what produced the warning. Every case now gets its own HOME under the harness directory, asserted before any write.

Post-fix falsification: doctor separates all three cases (configured/broken/unavailable) where before it reported one thing for all three. Repointed this VM's helper off /tmp onto ~/.config/github-app/jwt.sh, removed /tmp/github-app-jwt.sh entirely, and re-verified git credential fill exits 0; the reported dependency disappeared only because of that change.

Make doctor distinguish 'no credential mechanism' from 'a mechanism that stopped working' rather than reporting both as broken. Observed: the first implementation's verdict order called a fresh VM with no credential 'broken', which is the incident that cost this fleet a push and would have sent the next agent hunting a helper that was never configured. A diagnostic that cannot tell 'never set up' from 'stopped working' still does not read the property it reports.

Probe the push credential with 'git credential fill' and discard its output, never with 'git ls-remote'. Observed: this remote is public (GET /repos/ikihsan/think-free answers 200 unauthenticated) so ls-remote exits 0 with no credential at all, which would have been F010 with extra steps; credential fill exits 0 with the real helper and 128 without it, and git's own complaint differs between 'helper gone' and 'nothing configured'.

Renumber on the side that has not been pushed, and record the collision in STATE.md rather than editing a closed event stream. Observed: seven collisions between two VMs in one hour, each costing a rebase; two happened mid-rebase because the other VM pushed twice while the first rebase was resolving. Editing the event stream to say so is exactly the mistake F013 records.

Keep the other VM's implementation of the generated-stamp rule and drop this VM's duplicate. Both VMs found the same clock-derived date defect independently on 2026-10-04; the landed version is named consistently across the three generators and never falls back to the clock. Shipping two implementations of one rule would be the defect, not the fix.
